The matrix \( A_y = c S \) with \( c = \frac{h}{4\pi} \) and \( S = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & -i \\ i & 0 \end{pmatrix} \) is the y-component of the spin-½ angular momentum operator, \( A_y = \frac{h}{4\pi}\sigma_y \). Its eigenvalues are real: \( \pm \frac{h}{4\pi} \). The eigenvectors are proportional to \( \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ i \end{pmatrix} \) and \( \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ -i \end{pmatrix} \), which are not the standard basis vectors. Therefore:

- (A) is false because the eigenfunctions are not the basis functions of the given matrix.
- (B) and (D) are false because the eigenvalues are purely real (imaginary part zero), not the values stated.
- (C) is true: \( A^2 \) is proportional to the identity matrix for a spin-½ particle, so any state (including the eigenstates of \( A_y \)) is an eigenstate of \( A^2 \). However, \( A_y \) and \( A_z \) do not commute, so an eigenstate of \( A_y \) cannot be an eigenstate of \( A_z \).

Answer: C
